record.tranche_reason: The study reports qualitative evidence that SAE latents can be interpretable but also polysemantic or feature-split, refining the claim that dictionary features are complete, canonical units. It does not test toy-model superposition.
record.gate_note: The claim-relevant results are the qualitative inspection of Pythia-70m dictionary latents and the reported feature-splitting case. The reconstruction-error sweep and dead-latent percentages evaluate the proposed method and its training, not the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: This is a methods post. It trains sparsely-connected CLTs and attention SAEs on Pythia-70m and reports how its own method performs: FVU against C, dead latents, and dashboards of its own latents. SAEs are used as a tool. The post does not test whether real models contain recoverable sparse features (V4) or whether standard SAE features are canonical units (V5). Its qualitative dashboards judge the interpretability of its modified dictionaries, which have many dead latents. The feature-splitting remark is one anecdote about these dictionaries' connections, not a test of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author calls the results preliminary and ambiguous. Reconstruction error falls with C. Latents and connections are often but not always interpretable. Dead latents, high excess FVU, memory cost and feature splitting remain problems. The author has not updated much on whether the sparse-connectivity approach is viable.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains sparsely-connected cross-layer transcoders and attention SAEs on Pythia-70m using learned binary masks. It does not use the toy-network setup or geometric measurements of the original superposition study.
record.method_sensitivity: The qualitative dashboard findings are reported for the C≈100 run; the post does not report how those qualitative findings vary across C.

fits_no_version.finding: In the C≈100 sparsely-connected dictionaries on Pythia-70m, latent attn_2/0 had 169 upstream latents. Most fired on "of" in different contexts, and no single computationally relevant "of" direction was found. The author attributes this to feature splitting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dictionary features split into granular directions, so circuit-level analysis may miss the single computationally relevant feature.

record.problems: The evidence relevant to the claim is qualitative and based on dashboard case studies, with no uncertainty estimates or reported stability tests. The author cautions that the results are ambiguous and that the work is at an early stage.
record.rows_left_out: The reconstruction-error versus C results and dead-latent percentages are omitted because they assess the proposed method's reconstruction and training, not the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: No toy models, geometry or sparsity transition.
Capacity explanation of polysemanticity not examined.
No test of features spreading across neurons. SAE recovery is not assessed beyond the method's own dashboards.
Completeness, stability across runs and canonicality not tested.

record.verdict_notes: Changed from the reader's tests/T5 to uses_without_test/T4. Every qualitative result concerns the author's own modified dictionaries, which have many dead latents and come from one run. The author also concedes the latents may give little more insight than standard SAEs' virtual weights, which was not checked. None of the rows is an independent test of V4 or V5.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, its geometry, and sparsity-dependent transitions are not tested.
The study does not test whether capacity pressure explains polysemanticity or whether important features get dedicated dimensions.
It notes polysemantic latents, but does not test alternative causes of polysemanticity or whether it is evidence for superposition.
The study inspects SAE/CLT latents in one model; it does not measure whether features spread across neurons. Generalization to other models is not tested.
It reports a feature-splitting example, but does not test feature stability across runs or establish completeness and canonicality generally.
The dimensionality or geometry of represented features is not tested.

rows.subject: EleutherAI/pythia-70m
rows.operation_detail: Qualitative inspection of dictionary latent dashboards and their activating examples
rows.value: Latents often seemed interpretable; examples included capitalized words following “of,” biographies, and news contexts.
rows.note: The post describes selected dashboard examples and characterizes the overall result as often, but not always, interpretable.
rows.check: This is a qualitative check of the study's own sparsely-connected dictionaries' latents, so it evaluates the proposed method rather than V4. There is no baseline or rate, only a few dashboards from one C≈100 run.

rows.subject: EleutherAI/pythia-70m
rows.operation_detail: Qualitative inspection of a dictionary latent dashboard
rows.measure: Whether the latent's activations had a discernable pattern
rows.value: The post reports no discernable pattern among these activations.
rows.note: This is a qualitative counterexample to consistent recovery of interpretable features.
rows.check: This is one polysemantic latent (cc_3/7) in the author's own method's dictionary. It is method evaluation with no rate, so it cannot bear on V4.

rows.subject: EleutherAI/pythia-70m
rows.operation_detail: Inspection of the upstream connections to a downstream latent
rows.measure: Whether the dictionary exposed a single computationally relevant “of” direction
rows.value: The latent had 169 upstream connections; most appeared to activate on “of” in different contexts, and the approach failed to find the single relevant direction.
rows.note: The author presents this as a feature-splitting example: many granular directions were found where one computationally relevant direction would have been preferable.
rows.check: This is a feature-splitting anecdote about the upstream connections of one latent (attn_2/0) in the sparsely-connected dictionaries. It concerns the method's ability to find a computationally relevant direction, not the stability or canonicality of SAE features across runs. It is better recorded under fits_no_version. The numbers_found value '1/1' is not meaningful.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
